title: Complete SSRF and private-network tests
description: Verify SSRF protection for tool and node connectivity probes, including DNS/IP edge cases, redirects, URL credentials, and the narrow XUI exception.
acceptanceCriteria: Private/local/link-local/metadata literals and supported DNS resolution outcomes are blocked for normal probes
Redirects are manual or revalidated so a public URL cannot redirect to a private target
URL credentials are rejected and probe errors are sanitized
The XUI test exception is explicitly scoped and cannot affect tools or arbitrary node routes
Tests cover IPv4/IPv6 literals, encoded/alternate forms where supported, ports, redirects, and exception boundaries

steps.details: Add negative and exception-scope cases before modifying `isBlockedTarget` or route logic.

steps.description: Read `ssrf.ts`, tools route, node test route, xui test route, fetch options, DNS helpers, and current tests.

steps.details: Tighten only demonstrated gaps, preserving the explicit XUI private-network behavior and no-credential-in-URL rule.
Run focused SSRF tests, auth/origin tests, custom harness, typecheck, and lint.

technicalNotes: Do not treat a DNS lookup alone as a complete SSRF defense if the connection can resolve/rebind to a different address; document the implemented boundary.
actualOutcome: 101/101 SSRF assertions, 9/9 mutants killed. Five real defects fixed: isPrivateIp returned false for every IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (::ffff:127.0.0.1, ::ffff:169.254.169.254), a bracketed v6 literal skipped the literal branch entirely because net.isIP is 0 for it, twelve reserved IPv4 ranges were dialable (incl. 100.100.100.200 metadata and CGNAT), a host starting with '-' reached ping as a flag, and the node-test route returned raw ssh stderr to the browser. The XUI private-network exception is now pinned by tests rather than a comment. DNS rebinding is NOT defended against; the boundary is documented in the module header and in the evidence.
